description.short: Rich, aromatic, classic Ceylon black tea — the quintessential balanced archetype of the island's high-grown craft
description.overview: Facing opposite Uva on the western mountain flank, Dimbula receives monsoon rains on a different schedule, giving a mellow, harmonious, floral-citrus flavor profile universally loved worldwide.
description.leaf: Dark brown, tightly twisted whole leaves
description.liquor: Brilliant reddish-amber liquor with a golden halo
description.aroma: Aromatic, floral-fruity, with subtle jasmine and citrus undertones
description.taste: Medium-to-full-bodied, perfectly balanced, lively without the sharp edge of Uva
description.processing: Plucking → withering → orthodox rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: One of the earliest regions where Scotsman James Taylor and fellow pioneers planted tea following the catastrophic 1870s coffee blight.
history.development: The immediate success of Dimbula estates proved to the world that Ceylon tea could replace the ruined coffee sector and dominate global markets.
history.modern: Today Dimbula is an anchor terroir for premium blends and single-estate offerings, valued for its quintessential balance.
interestingFacts: The collapse of Ceylon coffee in the 1870s due to the fungal pathogen Hemileia vastatrix paved the way for the island's rise as a tea superpower, with Dimbula at its heart.
James Taylor, revered as the 'father of Ceylon tea', conducted his seminal commercial trials in this central corridor.
